question.text: Under the SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations, what is the role of the "cut-off time" in NAV determination?

answer.text: It determines the applicable NAV for purchase and redemption transactions based on the time of receipt of valid application and funds
It determines the time after which the AMC cannot accept any new investments
It determines the deadline for the fund manager to complete all portfolio transactions for the day
It determines the time by which the NAV must be published on the AMFI website

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p190-p191), cut-off timing determines the applicable NAV for purchases/switch-ins and redemptions/switch-outs. For purchases, the additional condition is that funds must also be available for utilisation by the scheme before the cut-off; for redemptions, only the time of receipt of the valid application is relevant. Page 193 supports time stamping of applications at official points of acceptance to evidence the receipt time. The Trap: Cut-off time is not the time after which the AMC stops accepting investments — applications can still be accepted, but the applicable NAV shifts. It is not the fund manager's trading deadline or the NAV publication deadline. The concept being tested is which day's NAV applies to a given valid application. Note: Purchase rules (application + funds before cut-off) differ from redemption rules (valid application before cut-off), and time stamping at official points of acceptance underpins both.
